statements.subject: client
statements.description: Sending systems SHOULD NOT generate the optional list of hosts known as a source route.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Receiving systems MUST recognize source route syntax but SHOULD strip off the source route specification and utilize the domain name associated with the mailbox as if the source route had not been provided.
actions: recognize source route syntax in RCPT forward-path

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Receiving systems MUST recognize source route syntax but SHOULD strip off the source route specification and utilize the domain name associated with the mailbox as if the source route had not been provided.
actions: strip source route specification from forward-path
utilize domain name associated with mailbox as effective destination

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Similarly, relay hosts SHOULD strip or ignore source routes, and names MUST NOT be copied into the reverse-path.
actions: strip or ignore source routes in forward-path

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Similarly, relay hosts SHOULD strip or ignore source routes, and names MUST NOT be copied into the reverse-path.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As provided in Appendix C, xyz.com MAY also choose to relay the message to hosta.int, using the envelope commands MAIL FROM:<userx@y.foo.org> RCPT TO:<@hosta.int,@jkl.org:userc@d.bar.org> or to jkl.org, using the envelope commands MAIL FROM:<userx@y.foo.org> RCPT TO:<@jkl.org:userc@d.bar.org>
actions: relay message to next hop specified in source route

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Since hosts are not required to relay mail at all, xyz.com MAY also reject the message entirely when the RCPT command is received, using a 550 code (since this is a "policy reason").
actions: send 550 rejection response to RCPT command

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT transmit parameters other than those associated with a service extension offered by the server in its EHLO response.
